result:
I fixed all 11 rules in `pricebook.py` where the code didn't match the docstrings. To check, I wrote a script that builds the expected result from each rule's docstring and the shared rules at the top of the module. It compared all 150 rules over qty 0–299 and 9 unit prices. Before the fixes it found 11 mismatches; after them it finds none.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 07 | Marginal rule, but the discount used the full amount | `(qty - 30) * unit` |
| 14 | Rate was 13% | 12% |
| 32 | Marginal rule, but the discount used the full amount | `(qty - 100) * unit` |
| 39 | Capped the eligible amount, not the discount | Cap the discount at 100,000 |
| 47 | Whole rule, but the discount used only units above the threshold | `base * 8 // 100` |
| 56 | Started at 6 units | Starts at 5 (`>= 5`) |
| 72 | Cap only kicked in when the discount was over 20,000 | Always capped at 10,000 |
| 85 | Rounded the discount (`round`) | Floored (`//`) |
| 90 | Rounded the discount (`round`) | Floored (`//`) |
| 131 | Rate was 16% | 15% |
| 140 | Marginal rule, but the discount used the full amount | `(qty - 50) * unit` |

Rule 121 is written `qty > 5` instead of `qty >= 5`, but at exactly 5 units the marginal discount is 0 either way, so the result is the same. I left it unchanged.

STATUS: DONE
